HEADNOTE: Section 281B of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Provisional attachment to protect revenue in certain cases - Assessment years 2002-03 and 2003-04 - Pursuant to a search conducted at residential premises of managing director of assessee-company, officials of Excise Department seized certain documents, computer and cash - Officials of Excise Department freezed assessee’s bank accounts - Thereafter, assessee filed writ petition whereby assessee was held to be entitled to operate said bank accounts - On same day, ITO passed order under section 281B and provisionally attached bank account of assessee - Whether since department could not show any material to justify action of assessing authority under section 281B except stating that certain enquiries with regard to nature and source of gifts in favour of managing director were to be enquired into, said ground was wholly insufficient to invoke section 281B, and, therefore, action of Assessing Officer could not be sustained - Held, yes

FACT: The assessee-company was carrying on the business in the real estate and the petitioner No. 2 who was the managing director of said company was doing the business in Kirana goods. Pursuant to a search conducted at the residential premises of the managing director of the company, the officials of the Excise Department seized certain documents, computer and cash. The company was having a current account with the bank and also had four FDRs. Subsequently, the officials of the Excise Department freezed the said bank account of the assessee. Thereafter, the assessee filed the writ petition whereby the assessee was held to be entitled to operate the said bank accounts. The Excise Department in pursuance of the direction given by the Court informed the bank to release the freezed account. On the same day, the ITO passed the order exercising the powers conferred on him under section 281B. The said order was passed in order to protect the interest of the revenue as in the opinion of the Assessing Officer, a substantial demand was likely to arise against the assessee as a result of the assessment proceedings under section 153A consequent to the search and seizure under section 132A. The order was passed with the approval of the Commissioner.

In writ assessee’s case was that the exercise of power under section 281B was wholly unwarranted, illegal and arbitrary and in impugned order had been passed without their being any material in possession of the department to form an opinion that there was likelihood of a substantial demand against the assessee.

HELD: A bare perusal of section 281B would show that two conditions are necessary for invoking it. Firstly, the existence of ‘opinion’ of the Assessing Officer that for the purpose of protecting the interest of the revenue it is necessary to provisionally attach any property belonging to the assessee; and secondly, the previous approval of the higher authority concerned has been obtained before passing any order. Section 281B gives very wide power to the Assessing Officer enabling him to provisionally attach any property belonging to the assessee with the previous approval of the Commissioner if the Assessing Officer is of the opinion that for the purpose of protecting the interest of the revenue it is necessary to do so. [Para 8]

The Delhi High Court in the case of V.L.S. Finance Ltd. v. CIT [2000] 246 ITR 707/ 112 Taxman 295 has held that opinion means something more than mere retaining of ‘gossip’ or ‘hearsay’, it means the judgment of belief that is a belief or conviction resulting from what one thinks on a particular question. [Para 9]

headnotes.text: Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, read with rule 159 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Section 83 of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, read with rule 159 of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Whether during pendency of any proceedings under sections 62, 63, 64, 67, 73 and 74, Commissioner after forming an opinion that it is necessary to do so for protecting interest of revenue, can provisionally attach any property including bank account belonging to taxable person - Held, yes - Whether these steps have to be taken in such manner as prescribed under rule 159(1) which deals with provisional attachment of property - Held, yes - Whether revenue or authority concerned needs to apply its mind before power is exercised - Held, yes - Whether an order of provisional attachment cannot be as a matter of course, rather, it is one of drastic measures which authority may be compelled to take if situation demands for purpose of protecting interest of Government revenue - Held, yes - Whether to provisionally attach all bank accounts and that too those accounts in which there was hardly any balance would only cause undue hardship to assessee - Held, yes - Whether therefore, where there was hardly a balance of Rs. 22 thousand in two bank accounts of applicant which had been provisionally attached, impugned order of provisional attachment of said two bank accounts was to be quashed and set aside - Held, yes [Paras 29, 43, 49 and 51]GST : An order of provisional attachment under GST is to be passed after proper application of mind, and cannot be a matter of course

Provisional attachment  -  Bank account- Pre-decisional hearing - Respondent-assessee was registered under GST and engaged in construction and other taxable services - Department issued summons seeking evidence on supplies and invoices - On alleged non-compliance and investigation into ITC misuse, Commissioner passed a provisional attachment attaching a bank account - Assessee filed a writ petition seeking quashing of attachment and unblocking of ITC - Single Judge set aside attachment solely for want of pre-decisional hearing - Revenue filed a writ appeal confined to bank account attachment - HELD : Plain text of Section 83 did not mandate a pre-decisional hearing before a provisional attachment - Statutory language could not be supplemented by implication where Legislature had not provided such hearing - Post-decisional remedy existed under Rule 159 enabling objection and hearing for release of attached property - Since Rule 159 expressly provided hearing after attachment, it reinforced that Section 83 did not require a pre-decisional hearing [Section  83  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule  159  of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 11 to 13 and 15] [In favour of revenue]

Provisional attachment of bank account - Writ jurisdiction - Provisional attachment order of bank account was passed in Form GST DRC-22 under section 83(1) during pendency of proceedings under section 67 - Since an effective remedy was available against such order before Additional Director General (ADG) under rule 159(5) of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017 and writ petition was filed without exhausting such remedy by taking recourse to aforesaid rule, High Court declined to interfere with such order - However, petitioner-assessee was granted time to exhaust such remedy under said rule by approaching to ADG who would pass a reasoned order after granting them opportunity of hearing [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017 - Article 226 of Constitution of India] [Paras 2 and 5 to 9] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Search was conducted at business premises of assessee under section 67 - After detailed investigation, show cause notice was issued to petitioner and thereafter bank account of petitioner was attached under section 83 - HELD : Power of attachment can be exercised on initiation of any proceedings under Chapter XII, XIV or XV - Since in instant case, proceedings were initiated under section 67, this procedure falls under Chapter XIV - Even after amendment of section 83(1) with effect from 1-1-2022, power of attachment can be exercised on initiation of any proceedings under Chapter XV, which had been done in present case - Argument of petitioner that proceedings had been initiated under section 122, read with section 127 did not fall under Chapter XII, XIV or XV was liable to be rejected - Such attachment would be enforced for a period of one year [Section 83, read with section 67, of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Haryana Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Haryana Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 14 and 17] [In favour of revenue]

Provisional Attachment of bank account - Provisional attachment of Property - Revocation of Attachment - Writ petitioner was aggrieved by order dated 28.05.2024, pursuant to which respondents-department had proceeded to provisionally attach bank account maintained by it in exercise of powers conferred by Section 83 - Held: Rule 159 confers a right upon writ petitioner to file objections and seek revocation of a provisional attachment that may be made - Therefore, ends of justice would be achieved if petitioner would be accorded liberty to move and seek lifting of provisional attachment in terms of Rule 159 - Accordingly, writ petition was disposed of by permitting petitioner to move in terms of Rule 159 within a period of one week.[Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017][Paras 4-7] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank account- Pre-decisional hearing - Petitioner faced DGGI investigation for alleged fraudulent ITC and was arrested under Section 132(1)(b) and (c) - During custody, bank accounts were provisionally attached under Section 83 without prior notice - Petitioner urged violation of natural justice due to absence of pre-decisional hearing and offered security - HELD : Section 83 did not, expressly or by necessary implication, mandate pre-decisional hearing - Statutory scheme read with Rule 159(5) provided complete post-decisional remedy by objections, hearing, and reasoned order - Protective attachment could be invoked during pendency subject to safeguards under Rule 159(5) - Courts could not read into statute a pre-hearing that legislature omitted - Absence of prior notice, even during custody, did not vitiate action - Petitioner had efficacious remedy to file objections under Rule 159(5) - Challenge on this ground failed [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Para 20] [In favour of revenue]

Provisional attachment  -  Bank account- Lifting of attachment - One-year expiry - Petitioner challenged provisional attachments in Form GST DRC-22 issued under Section 83(1) attaching three bank accounts - Earlier order in same proceedings set aside attachment of one account - Attachments over remaining two accounts continued beyond one year from date of DRC-22 - Writ petition was filed against continuing restraints - HELD : Attachments had remained for more than one year - Under Section 83(2), provisional attachment shall cease after expiry of one year from date of order - Rule 159(2) indicated removal earlier or on expiry of one year on Commissioner instructions - Since attachments had outlived statutory period, continuation was impermissible - Provisional attachments dated 11.11.2024 over two accounts were set aside - Writ petition allowed without costs [Section  83  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Telangana Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule  159  of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Telangana Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 4, 6 and 7] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank account- Alternative remedy - Petitioner was investigated for alleged fake invoices, circular trading, and wrongful ITC through non-existent entities - Arrest under Section 132(1)(b) and (c) followed - Bank accounts were provisionally attached during custody - Criminal proceedings were pending and challenge to parallel proceedings was reserved for orders - Respondents pointed to remedy by objections under Rule 159(5) - HELD : Power under Section 83 was drastic yet intended to safeguard revenue where prima facie material indicated evasion - Allegations were intrinsically factual requiring adjudication in appropriate proceedings - Writ interference at investigation stage was unwarranted given efficacious statutory remedy - Plea of bar under Section 6(2) lacked material and attachment was not vitiated for want of pre-hearing - No case was made out for interference under Article 226 [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017 - Article 226 of Constitution of India, 1950] [Paras 23 and 24] [In favour of revenue]

Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, read with rule 159 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Section 83 of the Haryana Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017 read with rule 159 of the Haryana Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - By this writ petition, petitioner had challenged order of attachment of its bank account under section 83, read with rule 159 and contended that necessary concomitant for exercising powers under section 83, namely, 'opinion of Commissioner that it is necessary for protecting interest of Government revenue', was absent - Department submitted that impugned order was in consonance with Form GST-DRC-22 and as per that form, there is no requirement for recording reasons - Whether since petitioner was willing to abide by any terms and conditions as may be deemed appropriate by High Court, impugned order was set aside upon condition that fresh order would be passed by department in accordance with law, taking into account submissions made by petitioner - Held, yes [Para 15]GST : Where petitioner had challenged order of attachment of its bank account passed under section 83, read with rule 159, contending that necessary concomitant for exercising powers under section 83, namely, 'opinion of Commissioner that it is necessary for protecting interest of Government revenue', was absent, since petitioner was willing to abide by any terms and conditions as may be deemed appropriate by High Court, impugned order was hereby set aside upon condition that fresh order would be passed by department, in accordance with law

Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 read with rule 159 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Section 83 of the Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 read with rule 159 of the Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Competent Authority provisionally attached under section 83 bank account of assessee on ground that it had created bogus records and claimed input tax credit for discharging GST dues of about Rs. 121 crores - Writ court, held that as a sum of Rs. 5.68 crores which was lying in bank account of assessee was appropriated by department and assessee had also agreed to pay another sum of Rs. one crore against estimated tax dues of about Rs. 21 crores, there was no meaning in attaching bank account further and directed that attachment order was to be vacated - Whether as statutory rule 159(5) provides for a procedure, where person whose bank account has been attached can seek for lifting of such attachment and assessee had filed objections dated 18-3-2021 seeking to lift order of attachment under section 83 and as on date objections filed by assessee under rule 159(5) had not been disposed of by Competent Authority by passing a reasoned order, it will be too early for Writ Court to make an observation that there was no meaning in attaching bank account further - Held, yes - Whether writ appeal filed by revenue deserved to be allowed and order and directions issued in writ petition deserved to be set aside - Held, yes - Whether assessee was to be directed to submit fresh objections in terms of rule 159(5) and thereupon Competent Authority shall consider same and pass a speaking order - Held, yes [Paras 5 and 7] [In favour of revenue]GST : Where Competent Authority provisionally attached under section 83 bank account of assessee on ground that it had created bogus records and claimed input tax credit for discharging GST dues of about Rs. 121 crores, as statutory rule 159(5) provides for a procedure, where person whose bank account has been attached can seek for lifting of such attachment, assessee was to be directed to submit objections in terms of rule 159(5) and thereupon Competent Authority shall consider same and pass a reasoned order

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Post-provisional attachment right - Subsequent extension of provisional attachment after first order of attachment was because of reason that investigation against petitioner in respect of taxation of service tax and GST continued - There are different accounts referred to in provisional attachment order and exercising powers under section 83, branch manager of Bank, was directed to allow only credit/deposit into account and not to allow any debit or withdrawal - Investigation was continuing for a long time - Charge-sheet was also filed late in case of present petitioner and his release on regular bail was delayed - HELD : Attachment of bank account after expiry of prescribed period without passing fresh orders would surely be illegal in violation of rights of assessee for carrying on business under article 19 of Constitution of India - After expiry of one-year period as prescribed under section 83, it is incumbent upon authorities to release provisional attachment or inform bank by issuing a fresh order of provisional attachment when very purpose for which this exercise of provisional attachment was done was not completed - In instant case, after expiry of one year period, authority has issued fresh order of provisional attachment - Such action of authority, therefore, when challenged though needed to be looked at cautiously for this being draconian powers - Authority was directed to complete and wind up its Proceedings of investigation in three months also file charge-sheet had within a specific time period - Extension since had come by a specific order, very action of attachment was not interfered with [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Para 12] [Partly in favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment  -  Bank account- Lifting of attachment - De-freezing denied - Petitioner, GST-registered technology service provider in Gujarat, acted as TSP for Digihub, facilitating payouts through current account with virtual accounts at respondent bank - GST authorities, probing Digihub tax evasion, provisionally attached petitioner accounts under Section 83 - Second attachment order followed - Petitioner sought quashing and de-freezing - Department cited payouts from petitioner accounts to beneficiaries of online gaming/betting funds, discrepancies, 35,064 linked accounts under examination, and petitioner admission of not verifying Digihub credentials - HELD : Facts were undisputed - Record showed Digihub used petitioner platform and bank account for gaming or betting payouts - Petitioner non-verification stood admitted and reliance on undertaking from Digihub was insufficient - No effort was made to check website or invoices to ascertain business nature - Considering enormity of transactions and ongoing investigation, attachment was justified and de-freezing was declined - Writ petition was dismissed [Section  83  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule  159  of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 7 and 8] [In favour of revenue]

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Search was conducted at business premises of assessee under section 67 - After detailed investigation, show cause notice was issued to petitioner and thereafter bank account of petitioner was attached under section 83 - HELD : Power of attachment can be exercised on initiation of any proceedings under Chapter XII, XIV or XV - Since in instant case, proceedings were initiated under section 67, this procedure falls under Chapter XIV - Even after amendment of section 83(1) with effect from 1-1-2022, power of attachment can be exercised on initiation of any proceedings under Chapter XV, which had been done in present case - Argument of petitioner that proceedings had been initiated under section 122, read with section 127 did not fall under Chapter XII, XIV or XV was liable to be rejected - Such attachment would be enforced for a period of one year [Section 83, read with section 67, of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Haryana Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Haryana Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 14 and 17] [In favour of revenue]GST : Show cause notice was issued after initiation of proceedings under section 67; proceedings would fall under Chapter XV and, thus, attachment of bank account of petitioner was proper; such attachment would be enforced for a period of one year

Provisional attachment of bank account - Writ jurisdiction - Provisional attachment order of bank account was passed in Form GST DRC-22 under section 83(1) during pendency of proceedings under section 67 - Since an effective remedy was available against such order before Additional Director General (ADG) under rule 159(5) of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017 and writ petition was filed without exhausting such remedy by taking recourse to aforesaid rule, High Court declined to interfere with such order - However, petitioner-assessee was granted time to exhaust such remedy under said rule by approaching to ADG who would pass a reasoned order after granting them opportunity of hearing [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017 - Article 226 of Constitution of India] [Paras 2 and 5 to 9] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where writ petition was filed against order of provisional attachment of bank account under section 83(1) without exhausting remedy available under rule 159(5) of CGST Rules, 2017, petitioner was directed to exhaust statutory remedy first

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Post-provisional attachment right - Subsequent extension of provisional attachment after first order of attachment was because of reason that investigation against petitioner in respect of taxation of service tax and GST continued - There are different accounts referred to in provisional attachment order and exercising powers under section 83, branch manager of Bank, was directed to allow only credit/deposit into account and not to allow any debit or withdrawal - Investigation was continuing for a long time - Charge-sheet was also filed late in case of present petitioner and his release on regular bail was delayed - HELD : Attachment of bank account after expiry of prescribed period without passing fresh orders would surely be illegal in violation of rights of assessee for carrying on business under article 19 of Constitution of India - After expiry of one-year period as prescribed under section 83, it is incumbent upon authorities to release provisional attachment or inform bank by issuing a fresh order of provisional attachment when very purpose for which this exercise of provisional attachment was done was not completed - In instant case, after expiry of one year period, authority has issued fresh order of provisional attachment - Such action of authority, therefore, when challenged though needed to be looked at cautiously for this being draconian powers - Authority was directed to complete and wind up its Proceedings of investigation in three months also file charge-sheet had within a specific time period - Extension since had come by a specific order, very action of attachment was not interfered with [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Para 12] [Partly in favour of assessee]GST : Attachment of bank account after expiry of prescribed period without passing fresh orders would surely be illegal being in violation of rights of assessee for carrying on business under article 19 of Constitution of India and, thus, after expiry of one-year period as prescribed under section 83, it is incumbent upon authorities to release provisional attachment; if even on expiry of a year, very purpose for which exercise of provisional attachment was done was not completed, authority should inform bank by issuing a fresh order of provisional attachment

Provisional attachment  -  Bank account- Lifting of attachment - limitation period - Petitioner ran footwear shop at Paramakudi - Business stood in spouse name - Petitioner maintained savings bank account with third respondent bank - First respondent issued provisional attachment under Section 83 attaching bank account, pursuant to which bank froze account - Petitioner challenged attachment contending that under Section 83(2) such attachment ceased after one year - Respondent did not dispute factual matrix - HELD : Statutory limitation in Section 83(2) mandated cessation of provisional attachment after one year - Continued freezing beyond prescribed period was impermissible - Impugned attachment was set aside and petitioner was permitted to operate account [Section  83  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10 to 12] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank accounts - Partial de-freezing - Assessee impugned attachment orders issued by respondent authority to bankers of assessee to attach seven bank accounts, being bad in law and without jurisdiction as basic ingredients of section 83 of GST Act had not been followed - Revenue submitted that, on investigation, it was found that assessee had availed ITC of 29.33 crores and had taken a refund of said amount - Assessee pointed out that to challenge aforesaid provisional attachment, it had already filed applications under rule 159(5) of CGST Rules - Assessee further submitted that respondent authorities be directed to unfreeze bank account of assessee with HDFC Bank and also unfreeze account at SBI to extent of Rs. 70 Lacs for its day to day management and business - HELD : One account in HDFC Bank and another in SBI was to be unfrozen only to extent of Rs. 70 Lacs - For other bank accounts, no relief was to be granted to assessee [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 11 and 12] [Partly in favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment  -  Bank account- Writ maintainability - Following search on 10.03.2026, bank account was provisionally attached via DRC-22 dated 12.03.2026 under Section 83 restricting debit transactions - Summons dated 14.03.2026 and 18.03.2026 were issued - Written replies were sent, yet appearance was not made - Writ challenged attachment citing guidelines under Section 83 - It was recorded that guidelines existed and no specific flaw in DRC-22 process was identified - HELD : Search culminated in seizure and sealing, and provisional attachment of bank account was ordered to safeguard revenue under Section 83 - Petitioner did not invoke statutory mechanism for release or de-sealing under Section 67(4) and Section 67(6) - Section 83 empowered Commissioner to protect revenue and guidelines dated 21.02.2021 governed attachment - No infirmity in process was shown and efficacious alternative remedy operated - Writ petition was dismissed [Section  83  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Rajasthan Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule  159  of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Rajasthan Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 19 and 25] [In favour of revenue]

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Revocation of - Petitioner-assessee's bank account was provisionally attached - Assessee had approached Commissioner for revocation of attachment, which was rejected by impugned order - Petitioner contended that there was no reason to believe nor was there any tangible material for Commissioner to confirm provisional attachment of assessee’s bank account in exercise of powers under section 83 - HELD : On perusal of application filed by assessee it was noted that basic essentials, which were necessary to persuade authority to revoke attachment and to make out a case that opinion of commission for attaching bank account was not proper, was absent from application - There was substantial material for Commissioner to form an opinion to attach bank account provisionally - Whatever material was relied upon in support of attachment, and which formed part of pre-show cause notice was not dispelled - Petitioner had not contended that such material was not tangible material to form opinion to attach Petitioner's bank account nor such a case was made out in application filed by Petitioner for revocation of the provisional attachment - Thus, assessee having failed to even make out a prima facie case against provisional attachment, petition of assessee was to be rejected [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 4, 7, 8 and 9] [In favour of revenue]

Provisional Attachment - Blocking of bank account - Bank was instructed to "Block" account of assessee without giving any reference to section 83 which was meant for provisional attachment - Thus, assessee had no scope to file objection under rule 159(5) of CGST Rules, 2017 - Further, no proceedings against assessee were pending which was a requisite under section 83 - There was also no formation of opinion that provisional attachment was necessary - Revenue's plea, that foreign remittances against exports had not been received, was never put to petitioner - No action was taken by revenue in last two years and four months - HELD : Section 83 provides a time frame for enabling investigation to protect interest of revenue though it is not a period of limitation - In instant case blocking order did not comply with jurisdictional pre-requisites which are embedded in section 83 - Hence, Bank account of assessee was to be unblocked [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 14.1,15 to 17] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional Attachment - Attachment of bank account - Show Cause Notice was issued against petitioner-assessee by respondent-department under Section 83 - Respondent issued attachment orders on ground that petitioner had failed to discharge tax liability without any justification, further, respondent was of opinion that there was every chance that petitioner might default in paying ultimate tax, interest and penalty, for which a demand might be raised in assessment proceedings on completion - Petitioner filed instant writ petition seeking setting aside of bank account attachment order issued by respondent - Held:Supreme Court had opined that power to order a provisional attachment [under Section 83] of property of taxable person, including a bank account, was draconian in nature and conditions which were prescribed by statute for a valid exercise of power must be strictly followed - Further, apex court had further opined that exercise of power for ordering a provisional attachment must be preceded by formation of an opinion by Commissioner that “it is necessary so to do” for purpose of protecting interest of government revenue - Expression “necessary so to do for protecting government revenue” implicates that interests of government revenue could not be protected without ordering a provisional attachment - As aforesaid order applies with full force to facts of present case, therefore, attachments in FORM GST DRC-22 dated 05.04.2024 and order passed under Section 83 also dated 05.04.2024 were to be quashed [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 3-6] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment of bank accounts - ITC fraud - ITC fraud was alleged against third party - Savings bank accounts of petitioners were provisionally attached - Petitioners submitted that advances and loans that were extended by them to said accused years back and funds received by them from accused were merely return of same - Petitioners annexed statement of their accounts of 9 years indicating withdrawal of sufficient amount from accounts of petitioners in favour of accused - HELD : Power under section 83 to provisionally attach assets or bank accounts is limited to attaching bank accounts and assets of taxable persons and persons specified under section 122(1A) - It is not open for department to attach bank accounts of other persons on a mere assumption that funds therein are owned by any taxable person - Since petitioners were not taxable persons or persons as specified in section 122(1A), impugned attachment order was to be set aside [Section 83, read with section 122 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 16 and 17] [Against Revenue]

GST : Where on spot visit, flying squad opined that purchases made by writ-applicant from two parties were not genuine and hence, collected documents and books of account and passed order of provisional attachment of two bank accounts, having regard to fact that there was hardly a balance of Rs.22,065 in two bank accounts, there was no good reason to continue provisional attachment   The avowed object of exercise of power under section 83 for the purpose of provisional attachment of any property is to protect the interest of the Revenue.Ultimately, if sufficient material surfaces indicating the involvement of the writ-applicant in some bogus transaction, the next step in the process can always be a show-cause notice under section 73 or Section 74 of the Act, as the case may be. However, to provisionally attach all the bank accounts and that too those accounts in which there is hardly any balance would only cause undue hardship to the assessee   An order of provisional attachment cannot be as a matter of course. It is one of the drastic measures which the authority may be compelled to take if the situation demands for the purpose of protecting the interest of the Government Revenue.   When there are plethora of judgments explaining Section 83 in details, then why so much of litigation in the High Court. The only reason that can be attributed is the mechanical exercise of power under section 83 of the Act. This should stop at the earliest.   Union of India as well as CBDT were directed to issue appropriate instructions or guidelines at the earliest with respect to the exercise of power under section 83

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Revocation of - Petitioner-assessee's bank account was provisionally attached - Assessee had approached Commissioner for revocation of attachment, which was rejected by impugned order - Petitioner contended that there was no reason to believe nor was there any tangible material for Commissioner to confirm provisional attachment of assessee’s bank account in exercise of powers under section 83 - HELD : On perusal of application filed by assessee it was noted that basic essentials, which were necessary to persuade authority to revoke attachment and to make out a case that opinion of commission for attaching bank account was not proper, was absent from application - There was substantial material for Commissioner to form an opinion to attach bank account provisionally - Whatever material was relied upon in support of attachment, and which formed part of pre-show cause notice was not dispelled - Petitioner had not contended that such material was not tangible material to form opinion to attach Petitioner's bank account nor such a case was made out in application filed by Petitioner for revocation of the provisional attachment - Thus, assessee having failed to even make out a prima facie case against provisional attachment, petition of assessee was to be rejected [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 4, 7, 8 and 9] [In favour of revenue]GST : There was substantial material for Commissioner to form an opinion to attach bank account provisionally whatever material was relied upon in support of attachment, and which formed part of pre-show cause notice was not dispelled

Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 read with rule 159 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/ Section 83 of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 read with rule 159 of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Competent Authority, exercising under section 83, had attached bank accounts of assessee - Assessee filed writ petition seeking relief in this regard - Whether assessee was to be directed to file objections under rule 159(5) against order of attachment before Competent Authority, who would decide such objections as expeditiously as possible - Held, yes [Para 5][In favour of revenue]GST: Where Comptent Authority, exercising under section 83, had attached bank accounts of assessee, assessee was directed to file objections against order of attachment before Competent Authority, who would decide such objections expeditiously

Provisional attachment of bank accounts - Principal Additional Director General merely stated that powers conferred on concerned official under section 83 was invoked for provisionally attaching bank accounts of petitioner in order to protect interest of revenue - However, order did not show any basis for formation of opinion that provisional attachment was necessary to safeguard revenue's interest - No tangible material was disclosed - Order breached mandatory pre-conditions for exercise of powers under section 83 ibid [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 9, 10 and12] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment  -  Bank account- Lifting of attachment - Conditional lifting - Petitioner challenged provisional attachment of bank accounts - Attached accounts cumulatively held about Rs. 10 lakhs then and at hearing - Petitioner undertook not to withdraw existing balances and sought operational freedom citing disproportionate prejudice and absence of quantified demand - Revenue alleged unbilled cigarette sales and wrongful ITC, claimed admission with part-payment; petitioner disputed any admission - HELD : - Controversy on alleged admission was not entered into - Petitioner’s undertaking to maintain existing balances was accepted and binding - Subject to such undertaking, attachment orders were lifted permitting operation of accounts - Banks were to ensure balances not reduced below levels as on attachment date or as of hearing date - Rival contentions were kept open and respondents could proceed against other properties in accordance with law; banks to be informed within three days [Section  83  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule  159  of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 13 and 14] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Petitioner, was a proprietary concern engaged in trading Gold Bullion and Gold Jewellery - Revenue issued summons under section 70 for an investigation and petitioner's business premises were searched, and documents, invoices, a mobile phone, and a pen drive were seized - Subsequently a second search was also conducted, during which gold bars, cash, mobile phones, and documents were seized and petitioner was arrested and, remanded to judicial custody - He was later on granted bail - Thereafter, revenue provisionally attached multiple bank accounts under section 83 of through Form DRC-22 - HELD: Provisional attachment was an extreme measure that must be based on tangible material and must be necessary to protect interest of revenue while instant attachment order was mechanical and failed to disclose any specific tangible material or justification for attachment - Since pendency of proceedings under Chapter XII, XIV, or XV of was not sufficient to justify provisional attachment and revenue did not establish that revenue could not be protected without attachment, impugned order of provisional attachment of multiple bank accounts was to be set aside [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 11 to 14] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional Attachment - Attachment of bank account - Show Cause Notice was issued against petitioner-assessee by respondent-department under Section 83 - Respondent issued attachment orders on ground that petitioner had failed to discharge tax liability without any justification, further, respondent was of opinion that there was every chance that petitioner might default in paying ultimate tax, interest and penalty, for which a demand might be raised in assessment proceedings on completion - Petitioner filed instant writ petition seeking setting aside of bank account attachment order issued by respondent - Held:Supreme Court had opined that power to order a provisional attachment [under Section 83] of property of taxable person, including a bank account, was draconian in nature and conditions which were prescribed by statute for a valid exercise of power must be strictly followed - Further, apex court had further opined that exercise of power for ordering a provisional attachment must be preceded by formation of an opinion by Commissioner that “it is necessary so to do” for purpose of protecting interest of government revenue - Expression “necessary so to do for protecting government revenue” implicates that interests of government revenue could not be protected without ordering a provisional attachment - As aforesaid order applies with full force to facts of present case, therefore, attachments in FORM GST DRC-22 dated 05.04.2024 and order passed under Section 83 also dated 05.04.2024 were to be quashed [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 3-6] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where petitioner-assessee challenged provisional attachment of bank account under Section 83 and apex court held that provisional attachment of bank account could only take place if it was necessary so to do for purpose of protecting interest of government revenue, therefore, following aforesaid judgement, provisional attachment order was to be set aside

Provisional attachment  -  Bank account- Lifting of attachment - Attachment during remand - Period 2019-20 - Following confirmation of demand under adjudication order and non payment respondents initiated recovery - Provisional attachment of bank account was ordered in Form GST DRC 22 under power of attachment - Writ petition also assailed subsistence of attachment pending remand - HELD : Attachment had been effected in furtherance of recovery linked to impugned adjudication - Since impugned adjudication stood set aside and matter was remanded subject to conditions continuation of attachment was not warranted at this stage - Predicate for attachment thus ceased during remand window - Respondents were directed to forthwith lift provisional attachment of petitioner bank account as per DRC 22 order - Clarification was issued that this order was confined to present procedural stage and did not decide merits - Rights and contentions of parties in de novo proceedings were preserved [Section  83  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule  159  of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 13 and 14] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment of bank accounts - ITC fraud - ITC fraud was alleged against third party - Savings bank accounts of petitioners were provisionally attached - Petitioners submitted that advances and loans that were extended by them to said accused years back and funds received by them from accused were merely return of same - Petitioners annexed statement of their accounts of 9 years indicating withdrawal of sufficient amount from accounts of petitioners in favour of accused - HELD : Power under section 83 to provisionally attach assets or bank accounts is limited to attaching bank accounts and assets of taxable persons and persons specified under section 122(1A) - It is not open for department to attach bank accounts of other persons on a mere assumption that funds therein are owned by any taxable person - Since petitioners were not taxable persons or persons as specified in section 122(1A), impugned attachment order was to be set aside [Section 83, read with section 122 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 16 and 17] [Against Revenue]GST : Where ITC fraud was alleged against third party and petitioners claiming to be creditors were neither taxable persons nor persons as specified in section 122(1A), order provisionally attaching their bank account was to be set aside

Provisional attachment  -  Bank account- Lifting of attachment - Petitioner challenged provisional attachment of its bank accounts under Section 83 - DRC-22 recorded that Section 74 proceedings had been launched and froze PAN-linked accounts - A writ was filed before High Court - HELD: Section 83 applies only to protect revenue on a reasoned opinion based on tangible material - This draconian power requires cogent reasons - letters contain only a bald assertion of Section 74 proceedings, with no specific grounds - In fact, no proceedings under Section 74 were initiated - attachments are perverse, arbitrary and without basis in law - Provisional attachment notices dated 23 July 2025 are quashed and release directed within 48 hours, liberty to proceed afresh [Section  83,  read with section  74,  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Uttar Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 7 to 11] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Provisional attachment order was passed attaching bank account of assessee - Assessee challenged same primarily on grounds that it lacked a Document Identification Number (DIN), that no proceedings under section 74 had been initiated, and that no reasons were provided for attachment - Revenue's case was that total tax payable by assessee was Rs. 2.21 crore while assessee had on its own, paid Rs. 98.92 lakhs, therefore, there was shortfall of Rs. 1.20 crore - HELD : Attaching a bank account is a significant intrusion into a citizen's private affairs and must be justified by compelling reasons - Assessee had voluntarily paid an amount, acknowledging tax liability - Said order of provisional attachment was not justified, especially without issuance of show cause notice and passing any adjudication order - Said order being highly oppressive and violative of articles 14 and 21 of Constitution was to be set aside [Section 83, read with section 74, of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Telangana Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Telangana Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 5 to 8] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional Attachment - Blocking of bank account - Bank was instructed to "Block" account of assessee without giving any reference to section 83 which was meant for provisional attachment - Thus, assessee had no scope to file objection under rule 159(5) of CGST Rules, 2017 - Further, no proceedings against assessee were pending which was a requisite under section 83 - There was also no formation of opinion that provisional attachment was necessary - Revenue's plea, that foreign remittances against exports had not been received, was never put to petitioner - No action was taken by revenue in last two years and four months - HELD : Section 83 provides a time frame for enabling investigation to protect interest of revenue though it is not a period of limitation - In instant case blocking order did not comply with jurisdictional pre-requisites which are embedded in section 83 - Hence, Bank account of assessee was to be unblocked [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 14.1,15 to 17] [In favour of assessee]GST : Petitioner's bank account could not be blocked vide communication which did not advert to section 83 of Central Goods and services Act, 2017

Provisional attachment of bank accounts - Principal Additional Director General merely stated that powers conferred on concerned official under section 83 was invoked for provisionally attaching bank accounts of petitioner in order to protect interest of revenue - However, order did not show any basis for formation of opinion that provisional attachment was necessary to safeguard revenue's interest - No tangible material was disclosed - Order breached mandatory pre-conditions for exercise of powers under section 83 ibid [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 9, 10 and12] [In favour of assessee]GST : Order of provisional attachment of bank accounts of assessee was not sustainable as it was passed without disclosing any specific reason based on tangible material available with revenue

Provisional Attachment - Jurisdiction - Petition challenges provisional attachment of their bank account by revenue under section 83 - Impugned provisional order of attachment in Form GST DRC 22 is non est in law as it revealed from impugned attachment order which was not in proper format as per Rule 159(1) of CGST Rules - Attachment was illegal, arbitrary, and without jurisdiction, and order did not follow the prescribed format - HELD: Part of cause of action arose within territorial jurisdiction of instant Court since petitioner's bank account in Kolkata was attached though may it be by an authority in Guwahati and in view of fact that petitioner was a registered person in Kolkata and as such writ petition before instant Court against impugned order passed by authority at Guwahati was maintainable and in view of section 6(1), Section 83, Section 122(1) and Section 122 (1A), Clause (i), (ii), (vii) and (ix) attaching bank account of petitioner provisionally and impugned order to this effect was very much legal, valid and within jurisdiction and was not liable to be interfered - Therefore writ petitioner was to be dismissed [Section 83, read with section 122 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 41 and 42 ][In favour of revenue]

Provisional attachment - Bank Account - Lifting of attachment - Assessee's bank account was directed to be provisionally attached on 27-1-2022 - Assessee submitted that in terms of section 83 (2), provisional attachment ceased to have effect after expiry of one year from date order of attachment was made - Respondent authority conceded that no fresh attachment order had been issued thereafter - HELD : Provisional attachment of bank account of assessee ceased to have effect - Bank should permit operation of said bank account [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 4 and 5] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Lifting of attachment - Bank account was directed to be provisionally attached on 27-1-2022 - Assessee submitted that in terms of section 83(2), provisional attachment ceased to have effect after expiry of one year from date on which order of attachment was made - Respondent authority informed that no fresh attachment order had been issued thereafter - HELD : In view of facts, Provisional attachment of account of assessee ceased to have effect - Bank should permit operation of bank account [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 4 and 5] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment  -  Bank account- Lifting of attachment - Conditional lifting - Petitioner challenged provisional attachment order attaching bank accounts under provisional attachment power - Respondent had conducted search and seizure, issued summons, alleged non-cooperation, and asserted GST-liable activities - Petitioner had produced invoices for scrutiny - Writ petition was filed - HELD : Considering rival claims and ongoing scrutiny of invoices, mitigating measures to safeguard revenue were invited - Petitioner offered to furnish fixed deposit of Rs. 1.5 crores in favour of Registrar General for permission to operate attached bank accounts and demonstrated bona fides by earlier deposit - Accordingly, attachment order was quashed to that extent and operation of accounts was permitted subject to fixed deposit - It was clarified that investigation would continue and show cause notice could be issued within reasonable period - Fixed deposit lying with Registrar General would be adjustable against crystallised liability upon finality, and if outcome favoured petitioner, release with accrued interest would follow - Amount of Rs. 1.5 crores was recorded as rough calculation pending final adjudication [Section  83  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule  159  of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 11 to 15] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment- Renewal/Revival of attachment - Assessee was subjected to provisional attachment under section 83 for 4th time - Assessee challenged same vide instant petition relying on judgement of supreme court in Kesari Nandan Mobile v. Asstt. CST [2025] 177 taxmann.com 481 (SC) - HELD: Supreme Court in Kesari Nandan (supra) clearly held that when statute does not provide for an extension, renewal, reissuance, revival, same cannot be done by authorities and such an action would amount executive overreaching statute - In light of same, impugned order attaching bank account of assessee was to be quashed and set aside - Authorities were to be directed to immediately de-freeze bank account of assessee [Section  83  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Uttar Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 8 and 9] [In favour of assessee]

Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 read with rule 159 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Section 83 of the Odisha Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 read with rule 159 of the Odisha Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Competent Authority by an order passed under section 83 provisionally attached bank account of assessee - Whether assessee was to be directed to file an objection to order of provisional attachment of its bank account before Competent Authority, who shall pass a reasoned order in terms of section 83 and rule 159(5) and (6) - Held, yes [Para 6] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where Competent Authority provisionally attached bank account of assessee, assessee was to be directed to file an objection before Competent Authority, who shall pass a reasoned order in terms of section 83 and rule 159(5) and (6)

Provisional attachment  -  Bank account- Lifting of attachment - Natural justice - Petitioner, a software company with operations in USA and India, was linked to DGGI Meerut probe concerning Redmil Business Mall India Pvt. Ltd. and Betterbot Tech Services Pvt. Ltd. - Summons dated 1 September 2025 and 8 September 2025 were issued to Director Finance for evidence and records - On 8 September 2025 ADG DGGI Meerut issued provisional attachment freezing eleven ICICI accounts, identifying one account and directing debit freeze on any account operated on same PAN - On 13 September 2025 petitioner sought withdrawal and personal hearing and hearing occurred on 23 September 2025 - By letter dated 25 September 2025 signed by Deputy Director DGGI objections were rejected and petitioner stated communication reached on 4 November 2025 - Preliminary probe alleged fraudulent ITC of about Rs 3.1 crores and petitioner deposited about Rs 40 lakhs - HELD : Petitioner was only a witness and no probe had commenced against petitioner - Freezing order preceded any response to summons and rejection letter was unreasoned, reflecting non-application of mind - Non-communication till 4 November 2025 violated natural justice and impeded remedies - Attachment of eleven accounts for alleged ITC of Rs 3.1 crores was prima facie disproportionate with debilitating business impact - Provisional attachment could not be continued at this stage and petitioner could operate accounts subject to maintaining Rs 1 crore in any attached account [Section  83,  read with section  169  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule  159  of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 15 to 17 and 22] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Petitioner had challenged order of provisional attachment of bank account dated 15-3-2022 under section 83 – HELD : As per section 83, every provisional attachment shall cease to have effect after expiry of a period of one year from date of order made under sub-section - Therefore, orders of attachment were self-limiting - They were to remain in force for one year - In view of above, writ petition was closed as nothing further survived for adjudication [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 3 to 5]In favour of revenue]

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Current account and Cash credit account - Communication in Form DRC-22 was addressed by Principal Commissioner to Bank Manager directing that proceedings had been lodged against petitioner under section 83 of CGST Act and, therefore, current account of petitioner was to be provisionally attached - Petitioner submitted that by virtue of attachment of account, apart from debit transfers all accounts were debit freezed - Not only current account, but in fact cash credit account was also provisionally attached - On writ, HELD : On more than one occasion, Court had deprecated practice of respondent authorities in seeking to enforce tax liabilities by provisionally attaching cash credit account - Notice was issued to respondent/s - Till returnable date, there would be ad-interim relief [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 5, 6 and 7] [In favour of assessee]

Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 read with rule 159 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Section 83 of the Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 read with rule 159 of the Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Competent Authority had provisionally attached assessee's bank account - Assessee filed writ petition seeking directions to Competent Authority to de-freeze/withdraw restrictions placed on operations of bank account - Subsequently assessee sought leave to withdraw petition with liberty to file objection in terms of rule 159(2) - Whether leave with liberty as prayed for deserved to be granted to assessee - Held, yes [Para 5] [In favour of assessee]GST: Where assessee against provisionally attachment of its bank account filed writ petition and subsequent it sought leave to withdraw petition with liberty to file objection in terms of rule 159(2), leave with liberty as prayed for deserved to be granted

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Provisional attachment order was passed attaching bank account of assessee - Assessee challenged same primarily on grounds that it lacked a Document Identification Number (DIN), that no proceedings under section 74 had been initiated, and that no reasons were provided for attachment - Revenue's case was that total tax payable by assessee was Rs. 2.21 crore while assessee had on its own, paid Rs. 98.92 lakhs, therefore, there was shortfall of Rs. 1.20 crore - HELD : Attaching a bank account is a significant intrusion into a citizen's private affairs and must be justified by compelling reasons - Assessee had voluntarily paid an amount, acknowledging tax liability - Said order of provisional attachment was not justified, especially without issuance of show cause notice and passing any adjudication order - Said order being highly oppressive and violative of articles 14 and 21 of Constitution was to be set aside [Section 83, read with section 74, of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Telangana Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Telangana Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 5 to 8] [In favour of assessee]GST : Total tax payable by assessee was Rs. 2.21 crore while assessee had on its own, paid Rs. 98.92 lakhs, provisional attachment order attaching assessee's bank account was not justified, especially before issuance of show cause notice and passing any adjudication order

Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, read with rule 159 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Section 83 of the Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, read with rule 159 of the Delhi Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Assessee filed writ petition challenging provisional attachment order dated 5-3-2020 issued by Commissioner to assessee's bankers - Whether keeping in view decision of Gujarat High Court rendered in similar circumstances in case of Pranit Hem Desai v. Additional Director General [2019] 105 taxmann.com 42 (Guj.) Commissioner was to be directed to treat writ petition as an objection under rule 159(5) and decide same within three weeks - Held, yes [Para 9] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where assessee filed writ petition challenging provisional attachment order issued by Commissioner to assessee's bankers, Commissioner was to be directed to treat petition as an objection under rule 159(5) and decide same

II Section 83 of the Central Goods and Service Tax Act, 2017 - Demands and recovery -  Provisional attachment - Whether on facts under heading 'Demands and recovery - Determination of tax' since nothing was demonstrated by department either in orders of attachment or in affidavit filed as to why exercise of such drastic power of attachment of bank accounts was necessary, provisional attachment of assessee's bank accounts was to be removed - Held, yes [Paras 16  17] [In favour of assessee]

Attachment of bank account - Revocation of - Jurisdiction to attach- Petitioner was partially responsible for allowing bank account to remain attached for long time and had not taken recourse to rule 159(5) of Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017- Since bank account was attached since April 2022, petitioner should approach Authority under rule 159(5) within one week and Authority should take decision within three weeks thereof [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rule, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017 - Article 226 of the Constitution of India] [Paras 3, 4 and 5] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment of bank account - Cessation of effect after one year - Assessee/Petitioner challenged provisional attachment of bank account under section 83 - Revenue provisionally attached assessee's/petitioner's bank account on 27-1-2022 - Assessee/Petitioner contended that as per Section 83(2), provisional attachment ceased to have effect after expiry of one year from date of order - Revenue conceded that no fresh attachment order was issued after initial provisional attachment order dated 27-1-2022 - HELD: Writ petition disposed of - Provisional attachment of assessee's/petitioner's bank account ceased to have effect after expiry of one-year from date of order - Bank directed to forthwith permit operation of said bank account and not impose any embargo based solely on provisional attachment order dated 27-1-2022 [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 4 and 5] [In favour of assessee]

facts.text:
The Competent Authority had provisionally attached the assessee's bank account by passing order under section 83.

The assessee filed a writ petition seeking directions to the Competent Authority to de-freeze/withdraw restrictions placed on operations of bank account.

Subsequently the assessee sought leave to withdraw the petition with liberty to file objections in terms of sub-rule (2) of rule 159.

■

Action under Section 2(9)(B) was initiated on the allegation that purchases shown by the appellant from M/s Sanmati Trading Co. were in a fictitious name. The property provisionally attached was the amount lying in the appellant’s bank account.

■

The IO recorded that the appellant showed purchases from a non-existent firm and alleged payments through banking channels, but the bank account of M/s Sanmati Trading Co. could not be traced and the appellant did not disclose it. The IO noted contemporaneous cash deposits in the account of M/s Asian Fabric around the same time as the payments to M/s Sanmati Trading Co., indicating routing/rounding of money back to the appellant. On this basis, the IO provisionally attached the amount involved in the benami transaction in the appellant’s bank account.

■

The Adjudicating Authority confirmed the provisional attachment of the amount in the appellant’s bank account.

■

On appeal to the Tribunal.

■

During the demonetization period, a survey under section 133A of the Income-tax Act was conducted on 21-12-2021 at Axis Bank. Multiple dummy accounts controlled by two groups were found to have received large cash deposits. Statements under section 131 of the Income-tax Act recorded admissions that cash deposited in these dummy accounts did not belong to them and was used to convert demonetized currency and was deposited by into the Green Traders account and, on his instruction, was transferred through RTGS to the appellant.

■

Based on the material, the IO initiated action under section 24(1) of the PBPT Act, recorded reasons to believe in writing, and issued a show cause notice. The IO analyzed sworn statements and bank statements, treated Green Traders as benamidar and the appellant as beneficial owner, and passed a provisional attachment order with a reference to the Adjudicating Authority.

■

The Adjudicating Authority, by order dated 29- 12-2023 under section 26(3), confirmed the provisional attachment and answered the reference.

■

On appeal to the Appellate Tribunal, the appellant contended that the section 24(1) notice was invalid for lack of recorded or conveyed reasons; that the Initiating Officer acted solely on borrowed information from the Income Tax Department; that sum received via RTGS was consideration for earth-filling work at Bhavnagar and the appellant was unaware of the proprietor of Green Traders; and that there was no evidence linking the appellant to depositing cash in Green Traders’ account.

The Competent Authority had attached provisionally under section 83 the bank accounts of the assessee.

The assessee filed a writ petition seeking relief in this regard.

It contended that the ingredients stated under section 83 were not attracted. The proceedings under section 62 or 63 or 64 or 67 or 73 or 74 were not pending consideration, which was one of the ingredients for passing attachment of bank account.

The revenue, on the other hand, relied on Annexure-D dated 27-8-2018 by which the assessee was asked to produce certain documents and the assessee had furnished the documents. Further the revenue relied on Annexure-E dated 17-10-2018 issuance of summons to the witness. The revenue submitted that both Annexures-D and E would fall under section 74.

■

The Initiating Officer issued notice and made a provisional attachment under section 24(3) of bank accounts with Andhra Bank standing in the appellant’s name.

■

Thereafter, while passing an order under section 24(4)(a)(i), attachment was made to a different property, namely a bank account with Axis Bank of one P.

■

The Adjudicating Authority confirmed the Provisional Attachment Order.

■

On appeal to the Appellate Tribunal :

The petitioners assessee challenged the provisional attachment order made under section 281B by the respondent Commissioner attaching the two immovable properties, bank account and FD Rs. with the bank. It was submitted by the petitioner that the valuation of these two properties was Rs. 5.83 crores as per valuation of the approved valuer as against the estimated tax liability of Rs. 2.68 crores There was no justification for attaching the bank accounts and FD Rs. which very seriously affected the day to day business of the assessee. The value of aforesaid properties as per Departmental Valuer was Rs. 2.66 crores. The petitioner submitted that the attachment order was unconstitutional unlawful, ultra vires without application of mind.

The Competent Authority, exercising under section 83, had attached the bank accounts of the assessee.

The assessee filed a writ petition seeking relief in this regard.

■

The appellant filed an appeal under section 46(2) challenging the order passed under section 26(3), whereby attachment of her bank account to the extent of Rs. 5 lakhs was confirmed while the immovable properties were released. The case arose from deposits of demonetized currency in the bank account of STC and transfer of Rs. 5 lakhs therefrom to the appellant’s account. The appellant admitted that the cash belonged to her and had been handed over for deposit in the bank account of STC and was thereafter retransferred through banking channels.The appellant further stated that out of Rs. 5 lakhs, she had paid Rs. 2.47 lakhs as tax, surcharge and penalty under PMGKY and deposited Rs. 1.25 lakhs in the interest-free PMGKY bond scheme, leaving a balance of Rs. 1.27 lakhs with her.

■

After enquiry, the Initiating Officer provisionally attached the appellant’s bank account and PMGKY bond deposit.

■

The Adjudicating Authority, while releasing the immovable properties, confirmed attachment of the bank account to the extent of Rs. 5 lakhs.

■

On appeal to the Tribunal:

■

The appellant filed an appeal under section 46(2) challenging the order passed under section 26(3), whereby attachment of her bank account to the extent of Rs. 5 lakhs was confirmed while the immovable properties were released. The case arose from deposits of demonetized currency in the bank account of STC and transfer of Rs. 5 lakhs therefrom to the appellant’s account. The appellant admitted that the cash belonged to her and had been handed over for deposit in the bank account of STC and was thereafter retransferred through banking channels.The appellant further stated that out of Rs. 5 lakhs, she had paid Rs. 2.47 lakhs as tax, surcharge and penalty under PMGKY and deposited Rs. 1.25 lakhs in the interest-free PMGKY bond scheme, leaving a balance of about Rs. 1.27 lakhs with her.

■

After enquiry, the Initiating Officer provisionally attached the appellant’s bank account and PMGKY bond deposit.

■

The Adjudicating Authority, while releasing the immovable properties, confirmed attachment of the bank account to the extent of Rs. 5 lakhs.

■

On appeal to the Tribunal:

The Competent Authority of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Department had provisionally attached the bank accounts of the petitioner under section 83.

On writ:

The assessee filed instant writ petition challenging the order passed under section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 whereby the various bank accounts of the assessee were provisionally attached. However, no further orders were passed for recovering any dues. It was submitted by the department that the inquiries had revealed that the assessee was a non-existing person and had not cooperated in the investigation and hence order of provisional attachment was justified.

■

After registration of the FIR, the ECIR was recorded by the respondent for having assets disproportionate to known sources of income and thereupon the investigation was conducted. The respondent thereupon provisionally attached the property belonging to the appellant finding it to be the proceeds of crime. The assets attached by the respondent was not only movable but immovable properties of the appellant and his family members. The provisional attachment order (PAO) had been confirmed by the Adjudicating Authority. Thus, aggrieved by the order, instant appeal had been preferred. The dis-proportionate assets to the known sources of income was quantified to Rs. 2.22 crore which was said to be 139.97 % to the income.

■

Appellant challenged said order on ground that after the PAO dated 23.12.2020, the order for its confirmation had to be passed within 180 days, otherwise the attachment would lapse as per section 5 of the Act of 2002. In the instant case, the order was passed by the Adjudicating Authority on 19.11.2021. It was beyond 180 days rather was after eleven months of the PAO. The prayer was accordingly made to declare lapse of attachment after expiry of 180 days from the date of the PAO.

■

The appellant further submitted that attachment order even included five bank accounts including an account where he was getting the pension. On account of the attachment of the bank account, the appellant was unable to get the amount of pension which otherwise could not be subjected to the attachment. Thus, on the aforesaid ground also, a challenge to the order of the Adjudicating Authority was made with a prayer to release the bank account, where the appellant was getting pension.

The Competent Authority for recovery of Rs. 3 crore from the assessee had provisionally attached its six bank accounts.

The assessee filed a writ petition stating that it had a large amount of cash lying at its disposal with the concerned banks.

The Competent Authority passed orders under section 83 of provisional attachment of goods and two bank accounts of the assessee.

On writ:
